This is a fifth pass at the PendingEntry/InflightEntry asymmetry from F1, now asking for branded types for a two-call-site invariant that is already documented in a comment. The agent declined; the reply-hint 'accept' is misleading.

narrative: A 12-round PR making TmuxTransport.send total. About half the 61 findings trace to earlier fixes. The dominant pattern is partial sweeps: the spawn stdin wrap missed ws.send (F8), the ws wrap missed failure recording (F21), the close-gate extraction missed the mock (F22), the mock migration kept a third format copy (F44→F46), and the format extraction left an open-gate hole (F52). Round 10 is entirely fix-caused; it includes a real regression where the F49 reversal broke F10's code-1000 clean-close semantics (F55). The agent also spent rounds declining to document two deliberate choices (the narrow InflightEntry type, the breaking signatures) until it eventually added a comment and a CHANGELOG, and it declined the websocket error-before-close finding twice before reversing on the same facts.
guidance_observations: Most avoidable findings came from fixing one implementation of a shared contract; sweeping every TmuxTransport implementation (spawn, websocket, mock) per fix would have removed four chains.

Recurring advisory findings on deliberate design choices stopped only once the rationale was in the code (comment, CHANGELOG); writing it there on the first decline would have saved several threads across rounds 2-9.
Reversing a decline (F27→F49) without rerunning the earlier fix's tests produced a regression (F55); a reversal should rerun the cases from the fix it touches.
Several no-op 'consistency' acceptances (F24, F59) added churn and, for F59, a possible re-entrancy hazard; findings the reviewer itself calls harmless should be declined.
